architecture_decisions: 4.1 Repository transition `WorkerExecutionRepository` owns a compare-and-swap transition from an unleased `FAILED` execution to `RECOVERING`. The transition must fail closed on concurrent state/revision/lease changes. It preserves checkpoint and lineage fields and the prior lease generation while resetting only worker-local anti-loop counters/fingerprints and current terminal recovery markers.

AC-01: validate protected requirement — An unleased `FAILED` worker continues to reject ordinary acquisition and autonomous dispatch when no explicit Engineering Run resume has re-armed it.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — After a successful explicit resume from Engineering Run `FAILED`, an existing unleased worker in `FAILED` transitions to `RECOVERING` with next recovery action `REASSIGN`.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — Re-arm preserves worker ID, checkpoint JSON/revision, current step, source lineage, last-known-good lineage and lease generation. Prior Engineering Run attempts/events are unchanged.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — Re-arm resets retry, no-progress and oscillation counters plus current/previous progress fingerprints. Prior stall classification and blocker are cleared from current worker state.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — The next protected durable-worker acquisition observes `RECOVERING`, invokes the existing reassignment path, increments lease generation once, and obtains a fresh mutation lease.
AC-06: validate protected requirement — A second human-resume preparation against a worker already in `RECOVERING` or later state does not reset it again or create another lease generation.
AC-07: validate protected requirement — PAUSED resume does not reset a healthy worker. HUMAN_REQUIRED, READY_FOR_INTEGRATION and SUCCEEDED worker states remain protected from this re-arm rule.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — `max_reassignments_per_work_unit`, validator-guided candidate repair, hosted Luna -> Terra -> Sol ordering, source-lineage authority, Git/provider/deployment ceilings and REVIEW remain unchanged.
AC-09: validate protected requirement — When run-event observation is enabled, the eligible human re-arm emits a worker RECOVERING event; historical FAILED events remain visible.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — Focused worker/recovery/API tests, full API regression, Bounded Autonomy, protected promotion and DSPy release gates pass on exact head. After exact-source production deployment, `/health` and `/ready` pass and a representative failed-run retry demonstrates a new worker generation can reach hosted implementation dispatch instead of stopping at the terminal-worker conflict.

critique: The human resume of a FAILED Engineering Run re-arms the terminal worker with exactly one new bounded worker generation, so the existing protected RECOVERING -> REASSIGNED path remains responsible for issuing the new mutation lease generation.
